result:
The plan change runs through `changePlanAction` in [src/actions/billing/change-plan.ts](/private/tmp/luna-scratch-20261008/211acde9-a30f-4137-aa8f-e2a2e5dad0e5/src/actions/billing/change-plan.ts). Its `withAction` wrapper first validates the request with `changePlanSchema`, then resolves the signed-in actor for the organization. `can(actor, "org:manage_billing", …)` allows an organization owner; `ROLE_MATRIX` in [src/lib/permissions.ts](/private/tmp/luna-scratch-20261008/211acde9-a30f-4137-aa8f-e2a2e5dad0e5/src/lib/permissions.ts) sets that permission to owner-level. Platform staff can also pass `can()`, provided the actor is scoped to that organization.

Before accepting the change, `assertPlanFitsCurrentUsage` reads current usage and compares it with the **target plan’s** limits using `wouldExceedLimit`. It checks seats, projects, and storage. Then `changePlan` in [src/server/services/billing-service.ts](/private/tmp/luna-scratch-20261008/211acde9-a30f-4137-aa8f-e2a2e5dad0e5/src/server/services/billing-service.ts) checks scope and authorization again and performs its own quota check: seats, projects, storage, and webhook endpoints, comparing current usage with the target plan’s quotas. Either check rejects the change if a checked resource is already over its new limit. The service-level check does not check issues per project or API requests per hour.

If the checks pass, `updateSubscriptionPlan` in [src/server/repositories/subscription-repository.ts](/private/tmp/luna-scratch-20261008/211acde9-a30f-4137-aa8f-e2a2e5dad0e5/src/server/repositories/subscription-repository.ts) writes the new plan and interval to the organization’s row in the `subscriptions` table, sets its status to `active`, and updates its timestamp. That subscription row is the stated authority for plan decisions: `planFor` in `billing-service.ts` reads it first and only falls back to `organizations.plan` if no subscription exists.

After the write, `changePlan` emits `billing.plan_changed` with the old and new plan. The event listeners registered by `registerEventHandlers` in [src/server/services/event-registry.ts](/private/tmp/luna-scratch-20261008/211acde9-a30f-4137-aa8f-e2a2e5dad0e5/src/server/services/event-registry.ts) record an activity entry through `registerActivityListeners` in [src/server/services/activity-service.ts](/private/tmp/luna-scratch-20261008/211acde9-a30f-4137-aa8f-e2a2e5dad0e5/src/server/services/activity-service.ts), and enqueue matching webhook deliveries through `registerWebhookListeners` in [src/server/services/webhook-service.ts](/private/tmp/luna-scratch-20261008/211acde9-a30f-4137-aa8f-e2a2e5dad0e5/src/server/services/webhook-service.ts). The action then revalidates the billing and organization cache tags. A deliberate plan change also ends any trial because the subscription update sets status to `active`.

There is an important gap between that authoritative subscription value and the rest of the product: this change does **not** update `organizations.plan`. Several non-billing flows read that organization column directly. For example, project creation, invitations, issue creation, attachments, webhook creation, and plan-based feature flags read it in `project-service.ts`, `invitation-service.ts`, `issue-service.ts`, `attachment-service.ts`, `webhook-service.ts`, and `feature-flag-service.ts`. Dashboard flag snapshots and `usePlanLimits` also receive `org.plan`. Those paths therefore continue behaving as if the organization had its old plan after this action. By contrast, `checkLimit` in `billing-service.ts` uses `planFor`, so the dashboard layout’s seat and project checks can reflect the new subscription plan even while the displayed organization plan and other gates remain stale. The event can also trigger activity and webhook handling, though webhook delivery eligibility itself reads `organizations.plan`.
